title: Returned Payments, Recent Declines and the Starting Step Percentage — Commercial Credit Account
content:
On a permanent increase of a Commercial Credit Account, two marks on the account's history decide where **the step percentage used** starts.

### Clause

The step percentage used starts from one half of the tier's largest permanent step percentage for an account that carries a returned payment entry dated less than the tier's returned-payment lookback in whole months before today and a limit request decided declined or referred to committee less than twenty-four whole months before today, from three quarters of it for an account that carries exactly one of those two marks, and from the whole of it for an account that carries neither.

Whole months between a date and today are the difference in calendar months, less one when today's day of the month is earlier than that date's day of the month, with no move of a month-end date to a shorter month's last day. The returned-payment lookback is 12 months on every tier; the decline or referral mark is read from the decision entries in the account's limit review history dated fewer than 24 whole months before today.

### Truth table

| Returned payment in the lookback | Decision declined or referred within 24 whole months | Starting point |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | one half (50 percent) of the tier's largest step |
| yes | no | three quarters (75 percent) |
| no | yes | three quarters (75 percent) |
| no | no | the whole tier's largest step |

*Hypothetical:* on a tier whose largest permanent step is 50 percent, one mark gives a starting point of 37.5 percent, and both marks 25 percent.
